description: Generates one voltage transition from an Init voltage to a Target voltage, timed in whole clock pulses and shaped by one of four curves

params.text: Sets the voltage the transition starts from, -10V to 10V; the setting is captured at the instant the transition starts
Sets the voltage the transition runs to, -10V to 10V; the setting is captured at the instant the transition starts
Sets how many clock pulses the transition lasts, 1 to 64 in whole steps, with the delay setting taken off the top so the two together never exceed 64
Starts a transition on the next clock edge, or at once when a clock edge has passed within the chaining window; a press is ignored while a transition or its delay is already running
Exchanges the INIT and TARGET settings
Steps the curve on by one each press, cycling Ramp, Ramp Back, Step and Triangle
Steps the start delay on by one each press, cycling OFF, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 clock pulses counted from the edge that arms the transition

inputs.text: Rising edges both start the transition and time it, one pulse to one step of the duration; if the clock stops the output holds where it is until the next edge
A rising edge cancels an armed, delayed or running transition and snaps the output back to the INIT voltage
A trigger starts a transition on the next clock edge, or at once when a clock edge has passed within the chaining window; it is ignored while a transition or its delay is already running

outputs.text: A 10V trigger 10ms long, sent when a transition finishes
The transition voltage; it holds the INIT setting until the first transition, and afterwards rests at TARGET for Ramp and Step or back at INIT for Ramp Back and Triangle

notes: Nothing happens until a clock is patched and a transition is fired, from the FIRE jack or the button. A fire before any clock edge has arrived arms the module until the first edge.
Every setting is captured at the instant a transition starts, so knob, curve, delay and easing changes made during a transition or its delay apply only from the next one.
The two-digit readout mirrors the DURATION setting, the DLY readout the delay setting and the icon beside them the curve; none of the three can be clicked.
The yellow lamp is lit from the moment a fire is accepted until the transition ends, covering the delay as well as the transition.
Only the difference between the two ease settings is used, so setting both to the same value gives the plain linear shape on every curve.
menu: Ease in — softens the start of the motion, 0 to 100 per cent
Ease out — softens the arrival at the end of the motion, 0 to 100 per cent
Same-step chain — treats a fire arriving within half a millisecond of a clock edge, or a quarter of the last clock period where that is shorter, as falling on that edge rather than the next one

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
